key_insight: Among four WC-10Co-4Cr spray processes, HVAF and HVOF produced the hardest coatings and best wear performance, while HVAF gave the strongest corrosion resistance.
engineering_relevance: The study helps engineers choose thermal-spray routes for wear- and corrosion-critical stainless-steel components by showing how process choice changes coating microstructure and service performance.
method: Applied WC-10Co-4Cr coatings to 304 stainless steel using APS, DS, HVOF, and HVAF.
Compared microstructure, hardness, friction/wear behavior, and electrochemical corrosion performance.
Ranked coating performance to identify the most suitable spraying route for different durability targets.
evidence_signal: Compared with 304 stainless steel, coating hardness rose to 771.4–1166.2 HV, wear rate dropped from 36.82×10^-5 to about 1.10–7.93×10^-5 mm3/N·m, and HVAF showed the best corrosion metrics (Ecorr -0.37 VSCE, Icorr 1.75 μA/cm²).
watch_item: Performance depends on spray-induced microstructure and carbide retention, so process optimization and coating quality control are essential before scaling to real parts.
paper_title: Microstructure, Wear and Corrosion Resistances of Atmospheric Plasma, Detonation, High Velocity Oxy-fuel and High Velocity Air-fuel Sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr Cemented Carbide Coatings
